title: Resulting rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of six lines. Start the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point zero three three nine, zero. Continue with the second line from zero point zero three three nine, zero to zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine. Draw the third line from zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine. The fourth line should go from zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two. The fifth line extends from zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two to zero, zero point zero zero two. Finally, draw the sixth line from zero, zero point zero zero two back to the origin at zero, zero. Apply a scaling factor of zero point zero three three nine to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles as the coordinate system, and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along its normal by zero point seven five units without extruding in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The dimensions of the resulting rectangular prism with rounded edges are length zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, width zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch points
p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
p2 = (0.0339, 0.0)
p3 = (0.0339, 0.0339)
p4 = (0.0319, 0.0339)
p5 = (0.0319, 0.002)
p6 = (0.0, 0.002)

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(p1[0], p1[1]) \
     .lineTo(p2[0], p2[1]) \
     .lineTo(p3[0], p3[1]) \
     .lineTo(p4[0], p4[1]) \
     .lineTo(p5[0], p5[1]) \
     .lineTo(p6[0], p6[1]) \
     .lineTo(p1[0], p1[1]) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-shaped angle profile extruded along X
leg = 0.0339   # leg length of the angle
t = 0.005      # material thickness
length = 0.75  # extrusion length along X

# Sketch the L cross-section on the YZ plane (normal = +X)
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, leg)
    .lineTo(0, leg)
    .close()
    .extrude(length)
)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

W = 0.0339      # leg width/height (Y and Z)
L = 0.7500      # length (X)
t = 0.0050      # angle leg thickness

# L-shaped cross-section in the YZ plane, extruded along X
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .polyline([
        (0, 0),
        (W, 0),
        (W, W),
        (W - t, W),
        (W - t, t),
        (0, t),
    ])
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)
